forward_patch:
--- original
+++ modified
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+---
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8180'
+title: 'Write-ahead record of a tool call: the .toolCalls entry reaches the recording when the call starts, not at the end of the submission'
+---
+## What
+After a crash during a tool run, the recording of the session must already hold the tool call that was in flight. This is a requirement of the user (2026-11-03) for resuming nested sub-agent sessions: a re-driven sub-agent must complete the ORIGINAL `start agent` tool call (same tool, same correlationID) of its caller, so that call must be in the transcript of the caller after the restart.
+
+Facts (from the Router session, 2026-11-03):
+- Today the transcript entries are written at the END of a submission: `finishSubmission` (`Session/RoutedSessionActorRecording.swift:34`) calls `recordTranscriptDelta` (line 280), which diffs the backend transcript against `persistedBaseline` and appends the partials. The `.toolCalls` partial and the `toolCall` + running `toolStatus` events (`emitSessionEvents`, near line 420) all come from that one diff, after the SDK tool loop ended. During the loop the entry exists only in memory in the backend.
+- Operation events (progress, elicitation, message, completed) are different: the outbox journals each posted event at post time (`Session/SessionOutbox.swift:15-20`, `journalWithoutStaging` near line 298). So a running tool run leaves non-terminal journal events on disk, but no `.toolCalls` entry. A run that posted no event leaves nothing.
+- Reading `LanguageModelSession.transcript` between tool-loop passes aborts the process (known; see `Session/RoutedSessionActorCompactionYield.swift` lines 185 to 208, `recordAttemptStoppedAtToolCall` and the in-flight rebuild). So the write-ahead cannot come from a transcript diff. It must come from the tool-mount layer (`ToolMounting.makeSessionMounted`), which knows the tool name, the call id and the arguments when a call starts.
+
+Do (design first, then implement; write the design in a task comment and discuss it with the user before the code):
+1. At the start of each tool call, record a `.toolCalls` entry (call id, tool name, arguments JSON) durably. One small partial for each tool pass is enough.
+2. Change the baseline handling so the later transcript diff at the end of the submission does not record the same entry a second time.
+3. A crash between the write-ahead and the end of the submission leaves the call in the recording without an output. Define how a restore treats an open call: the transcript must stay valid for the model, and the open call must pair with its later output (the `completed` event of the run, or `lost`). Check `ToolCallOutputPairing` and `TranscriptReconstruction`.
+4. A run that settled inline is unchanged in what the model sees after a clean end.
+
+Consumer: FoundationModelsACPAgent board, tag `subagents`, task "Re-drive interrupted nested runs after a cold resume" (`01M6GK6AX0RWQ1PDT89GC0991F`). A second Router piece is needed after this one and is not decided: a way for a host to claim an orphan run at restore so the restore does not post `lost` (`Recording/SessionTreeRestoration.swift:493-499`), and then post the real `completed`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] Kill the process during a tool run; after the restore the recording of the session holds the `.toolCalls` entry of that call.
+- [ ] A clean run records each tool call exactly once (no duplicate from the end-of-submission diff).
+- [ ] A restored open call pairs with its output when the run later completes, and the transcript is valid for the model.
+- [ ] The write-ahead write does not read `LanguageModelSession.transcript` between tool-loop passes.
+- [ ] No change in the behavior of an existing clean session.
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsRouterTests/WriteAheadToolCallTests.swift`: crash simulation (stop the session without `finishSubmission`), restore, check the entry; no duplicate on a clean run; open call pairing.
+- [ ] Run `swift test --filter WriteAheadToolCallTests`. All pass.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass. #subagents
\ No newline at end of file

@@ -1,4 +1,19 @@
 ---
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m6gt7e74tvhjgvrvkvdqknf1
+  text: |-
+    DESIGN (no code written yet). NEEDS THE USER: it adds a recording format kind and it reads the criterion "exactly once" in one way (see 2).
+
+    1. New partial kind `.toolCallStarted`: one per tool call, with call id, tool name and arguments JSON. It is written when the call starts, from the tool-mount layer (`ToolMounting.makeSessionMounted`), which knows these three values. It does not read `LanguageModelSession.transcript`. The write is one small append through the recorder (`append(partial:)`) and it is durable before the tool body runs. The live events `toolCall` and running `toolStatus` go out at that moment (earlier than today, same content).
+    2. The `.toolCalls` entry stays as today: the end-of-submission diff writes it. The two do not collide: `.toolCallStarted` is a different kind, so `persistedBaseline` and the diff need no change for the entry. The end diff skips the live `toolCall` and running `toolStatus` events for call ids that the started path emitted already (a set of started ids in the session actor, removed when the diff covers them). Reading of the criterion: "each call exactly once" means once in the RECONSTRUCTED transcript and in the live events; the file holds the small started marker beside the entry. Alternative if the user wants one record only: write the started entry as the real `.toolCalls` entry and make the end diff skip it. I reject it: one pass can hold several parallel calls in one SDK entry, whose id is not known at call start without reading the transcript.
+    3. Reconstruction (`TranscriptReconstruction`): a `.toolCallStarted` whose call id is covered by a later `.toolCalls` entry is dropped. A `.toolCallStarted` not covered is an OPEN call. The restore folds the open calls that follow the same prompt into one `.toolCalls` entry, and keeps the order.
+    4. The output of an open call, for the model after a restore: the transcript must have an output for each call. CHECK `ToolCallOutputPairing` and the SDK rule. Proposal: the restore adds a placeholder `.toolOutput` ("run still working") for an open call, as the inline settle grace does for a background run today, and the real result comes as run mail (`completed` or `lost`) from the journal or from a claim (card 01M6GK8K45DRDT6B4SHB9V60ED). This keeps the transcript valid and the model informed.
+    5. A run settled inline is unchanged after a clean end: the entry and output are the same, only the started marker is extra in the file.
+    6. Cost: one extra append per tool call. Measure it in the test (no time limit, only a count of appends).
+
+    Tests (`WriteAheadToolCallTests`): stop the session before `finishSubmission`, restore, the started marker is there and the open call folds into one entry; clean run has no duplicate in the reconstruction or in the live events; open call pairs with a later output; no read of the transcript between passes.

--- original

@@ -14,6 +14,28 @@

     Tests (`WriteAheadToolCallTests`): stop the session before `finishSubmission`, restore, the started marker is there and the open call folds into one entry; clean run has no duplicate in the reconstruction or in the live events; open call pairs with a later output; no read of the transcript between passes.
   timestamp: 2026-11-03T13:40:23.908210+00:00
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m6h3pwaw0a13bvq4a1r39s4f
+  text: |-
+    CHECK ANSWERS (read from the code before any change).
+    1. ToolCallOutputPairing: it pairs a .toolOutput entry to a call by id. The SDK sets Transcript.ToolOutput.id to the id of the call it answers (measured on macOS 27, see the doc of ToolCallOutputPairing). When the id names no announced call, the oldest call without output is used. So a placeholder output must have the id of its call.
+    2. SDK rule on outputs: no SDK text is in the checkout (it is a binary framework), so the rule is not proved by a test. The code of the session keeps the rule that each call has an output: InFlightTranscript.removingUnansweredCalls removes a call that has no output after a stop, and InFlightTranscript.appendingOutputs adds the output of each result. The restore follows the same rule: one placeholder output for each open call.
+    3. Background-run placeholder today: the tool answers with the rendered PendingRunEnvelope (JSON with pending, completionToken, next). It is a normal .toolOutput entry. TokenCappingTool never cuts it. The real result arrives later as run mail. The envelope needs a valid ULID completion token (makeDecoded checks it), and a restore after a crash has no token for the call. So the restore uses a plain text placeholder (OpenToolCalls.placeholderOutput), not an envelope.
+
+    CHANGES FROM THE DESIGN (the user or the coordinator must decide).
+    A. Place of the write: ToolMounting.makeSessionMounted does not know the call id. Tool.call(arguments:) gets no call id, and the decorator has no access to the session actor. The write is in RoutedSessionActor.deliver(invocation:) for the OPEN ToolInvocationRecord. The Extras mount layer posts it with await before the tool body runs, so the marker is on disk before the body. The id, the name and the arguments come from ToolCallRunJoin.openedCall (the SDK waits in the tool call, the same read as before, no new read between passes).
+    B. Live events at the start of the call: NOT done. Evidence: with the toolCall and running toolStatus events sent at the start, 4 existing tests failed. SessionObserverSeedingTests (grouped rows of the live projection differ from the seeded rows) and ToolInvocationLivenessTests (event order). Cause: SessionObserver closes the narration text of a pass (textReset) only when the last row is the open text row. A call row that came earlier hides it, so the narration no longer joins its call group. The live events stay at the end of the submission, as before. So no duplicate is possible and no consumer changes. If early live events are still wanted, SessionObserver must change first (card to add).
+    C. Fork: forkPrefix now drops a toolCallStarted marker that follows the last entry the fork keeps. Without it, each fork would inherit the markers of the next submission of its parent and show them as open calls (test in WriteAheadToolCallTests).
+    D. Existing tests changed: ToolInvocationLivenessTests expect the toolCallStarted marker in the recorded kinds (2 places).
+
+    OPEN POINTS. (1) A call that started and was cancelled (no .toolCalls entry ever) leaves an uncovered marker, and a later restore shows it as an open call. (2) A crash while call 1 of a submission is done and call 2 runs shows both as open: the result of call 1 is not recorded, and the placeholder text says so. (3) The prompt of the submission in flight is not recorded (entries are written at the end), so the folded entry follows the last recorded entry. (4) A fork of a restored parent does not inherit the open call of the parent that has no later entry.
+
+    Files: Recording/OpenToolCalls.swift (new), TranscriptEvent.swift, TranscriptEntryMapper.swift, TranscriptTree.swift, TranscriptReconstruction.swift, ContextRenderer.swift, SessionTreeRestoration.swift, Session/ToolCallRunJoin.swift, RoutedSessionActorRunJournal.swift, RoutedSessionActorRecording.swift, SessionObserver.swift; tests: WriteAheadToolCallTests.swift (new, 18 tests), ToolInvocationLivenessTests.swift.
+
+    ### implement - changed
+    - evidence: full swift test: 2280 tests in 277 suites passed, 0 failures; WriteAheadToolCallTests 18 tests passed (confirmed by the suite line in the log).
+    - next: review
